en: The Hymn to Śākyasiṃha composed by Surapati:
O Śrī Śākyasiṃha, benefactor of all, King of Dharma, Great Lord! [I praise you] with ships.
I bow to the Omniscient One, the Body of Wisdom, free from the three stains, the Son of the Sugata, the King of Enlightenment;

the Support of Dharma, the Lord of Sages, endowed with the power of the ten strengths, the Mass of Glory, the Universal Form, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Protector of the World, who dwells in the realm of mortals and removes all fear. (1)

You, who are the object of the faith in the Dharma resorted to by all the sons of the Jinas, and who thereafter attained the name Śvetaketu as the cause of enlightenment— O King of Enlightenment, you have come from Tuṣita!
Having installed Maitreya, whose mind was filled with joy, upon his own seat and having consecrated him,
he settled him within the pure womb of Māyā, which was free from impurity and defilement and adorned with jewels.

Even while remaining in the womb, you provide an exposition of the Dharma that brings benefit to all; and when born, you illuminate everything with your own rays from your mother’s side. Having performed the worldly customs and the ten prescribed rites, such as marriage and the rest, you act accordingly.
I bow to you, who have renounced everything, including the kingdom, and have gone forth for the welfare of all people. || 3 ||
From whose ūrṇā-kośa there daily and repeatedly issues forth a right-turning radiance,
which, blazing intensely, destroys the darkness of delusion within the hollows of the three worlds;
and who terrifies the denizens of hell with the forty rays of light streaming from his beautiful teeth.
I bow to him by whom [the earth] was lifted up and established in the heavenly world, which is adorned with celestial trees. || 4 ||

Those hands, marked with the sign of the wheel and granting desired fruits, having caused the Goddess of the Earth— who was radiant with the excellence of his perfection in generosity and surrounded by her own retinue—
to cleave that earth; and having stood before him and honored him, they rebuked the approaching Namuci, the enemy.
Standing as a witness and remaining hidden, I bow my head and pay homage to you, the Lord of Jinas. || 5 ||
Before whose uplifted neck the experts stationed in the worlds of Brahmā,
Śiva, and Viṣṇu lack even the power to behold him— how much less those like me dwelling in the city of mortals?
Having leaped across the cosmic egg, he has transcended the sun and moon, the heavens, and the realm of the stars.
I bow to you, who are resplendent in the supreme, innate world called the Transcendental (lokottara) situated above. || 6 ||
O Lord of the Omniscient, seeing Your face— which resembles a lotus, enriched with the teeth as its petals and the nose as its pericarp,
and within which the cosmic egg expands like a pericarp containing the circular array of all worlds—
Namuci became utterly bewildered; please protect him along with his followers.
Having made [others] go for refuge to You, the beloved Śrīghana, I bow down to You. || 7 ||
If all the scholars dwelling in the abode of the three worlds, who are experts in the knowledge of calculation, were to join together and describe your majesty for the duration of a kalpa,
they would still not be able in any way to reach the further shore of that ocean of milk which is your entire multitude of virtues.
Though she alone may not be capable [of this], I bow to you for the sake of awakening my mind. || 8 ||
The world-protectors, beginning with Śakra, along with their respective attendants, recite this hymn composed by the Lord of the Gods in the meter known as Sragdharā; they shall provide protection.
Having enjoyed happiness here in this world, one will thereafter [dwell] in the realm of the Lord of the Gods, strewn with wish-fulfilling trees.
Having remained there, they eventually go to the ground of the Son of the Sugata, which is accessible only to those who transcend the entire world.
The *Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra* composed by Surapati is completed.
